title: Identity, authorization and audit
summary: Who authenticated, whose permissions applied, where the request failed, and what the audit log can prove afterwards.
outcomes: Classify principals and provisioning mechanisms and predict how a membership change alters access.
Trace OAuth U2M, OAuth M2M and workload identity federation, and name the token exposure mistakes that bearer credentials invite.
Predict results under run-as identities, row filters, column masks and attribute-based policies, and place a failure at its layer.
Query audit rows as incident evidence and write a least-privilege plan with a test matrix and separated duties.
startingAssumptions: The Unity Catalog module's three-part names and the USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and SELECT grants are familiar.
The cloud bridge lesson separates identity, authorization and reachability on one request.
editorialRationale: Identity teaching fails when authentication, authorization and audit blur into one topic, so the module follows a request in order: which principal exists and how it was provisioned, how it proves itself through U2M, M2M, federation, tokens and secrets, whose permissions apply, what filters, masks and attribute-based policies do to the answer, and what audit rows can prove after an incident. It ends in the review artifact that the governance lab reuses, builds on the Unity Catalog module's grants without repeating them, and marks every detail whose source could not be confirmed in this build.

claims.description: Users are identities for people, represented by email addresses; service principals are identities for jobs, automated tools, scripts, apps and CI/CD platforms; Databricks recommends running production jobs as service principals so interactive users need no write, delete or modify privileges in production; Databricks-managed service principals exist on every cloud and reach only Databricks.

Groups can contain users, service principals and other groups; members inherit the permissions assigned to their group; assigning workspace access and Unity Catalog access-control policies to groups rather than individual users is documented best practice; account principals are assigned to a workspace with USER or ADMIN permission and receive workspace entitlements separately.

Databricks recommends SCIM provisioning to sync users and groups from the identity provider into the Databricks account, and terminating a user in the identity provider removes the user from the account; with identity federation enabled, user attributes are maintained through the account-level SCIM APIs rather than the workspace SCIM APIs.
claims.context: Provisioning and identity federation; connector specifics vary by identity provider.

claims.description: OAuth user-to-machine sign-in in the SDK's external-browser strategy runs an authorization-code flow with a PKCE challenge through the browser and a localhost redirect, requests offline_access for a refresh token and caches the tokens locally; after databricks auth login, tools can reuse the CLI profile's cached OAuth token, and every call acts as the signed-in user.
claims.context: Client behaviour of the SDK and CLI; server-side token lifetimes not stated.

claims.description: OAuth machine-to-machine authentication presents a service principal's client ID (its application ID) and an OAuth secret with the client-credentials grant at the Databricks token endpoint, discovered from /oidc/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; the SDK requests the all-apis scope by default, sends the bearer token on each request and refreshes it before expiry.
claims.context: OAuth M2M on account and workspace APIs, all clouds.

claims.description: Service principal OAuth secrets are managed by administrators and used to obtain OAuth access tokens for account and workspace APIs; without an explicit lifetime a secret lasts 730 days, and each secret reports its creation time, expiry time and status.
claims.context: Default lifetime as documented by the provider at v1.133.0.

claims.description: Workload identity federation lets workloads outside Databricks authenticate as a service principal by exchanging a token issued by their own runtime, with no Databricks secret; a service principal federation policy names the accepted issuer and the permitted subject, audiences default to the Databricks account ID, and Databricks strongly recommends it over OAuth client secrets or personal access tokens whenever possible; account federation policies extend token federation to users and service principals and are typically combined with SCIM.
claims.context: Federation policies at account level; GA badge on the provider resources at v1.133.0.

claims.description: Databricks strongly recommends OAuth instead of personal access tokens for user authentication; personal access tokens carry a lifetime set at creation; the right to use tokens is itself a permission (CAN_USE on the tokens object); on-behalf-of tokens for service principals exist on AWS and Google Cloud but OAuth is generally preferred; administrators can list and delete other users' tokens, and token records carry creation time, expiry time and an approximate last-used day.

Secret scope ACLs grant READ (read and list), WRITE (read and write) or MANAGE (also change the ACL) to users, groups or service principals; secret values are read only from within a command on a cluster, with the permission of whoever runs the command; values can be referenced as {{secrets/scope/key}} in Spark configuration and environment variables; Databricks redacts secret values shown in notebooks where it can but cannot prevent a permitted user from reading a secret.

A job runs as its run-as identity and, when none is set, as the user who created it; making a service principal the run-as identity requires the servicePrincipal user role, account rule sets separate the service principal Manager and User roles, and job permissions separately control who can view, manage, trigger or cancel a job.

Row filters and column masks are SQL functions attached to a table and evaluated at query time: a row filter, attached with SET ROW FILTER ... ON (columns), receives table columns and returns whether a row is visible, and a column mask, attached with ALTER COLUMN ... SET MASK, receives the masked column, with optional other columns, and returns the value to show, its first argument and return type matching the column; a query that meets them returns fewer rows or masked values rather than an error.
claims.context: Unity Catalog tables; supported compute and runtimes vary.

concepts.definition: A principal that represents one person, identified by an email address and normally provisioned from the organisation's identity provider.
concepts.example: maya@cinderline.example is a user; her grants arrive through the groups she belongs to.

concepts.definition: A principal for jobs, scripts, apps and CI/CD with no person behind it, identified by an application ID and authenticated with OAuth or federation.
concepts.example: sp-nightly-ingest runs the nightly load and is the identity Unity Catalog checks at the write.

concepts.definition: A principal that collects users, service principals and other groups so that a grant or entitlement is given once and inherited by every member.
concepts.example: quality-analysts holds SELECT on quality.accepted; moving Maya out of it removes her read without editing a grant.

concepts.definition: SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) provisioning syncs users, groups and memberships from the identity provider into the Databricks account and removes them when they are deprovisioned there.
concepts.example: Disabling Priya in Cinderline's identity provider removes her from the Databricks account on the next sync.

concepts.definition: The model in which users, service principals and groups live at the Databricks account level and are assigned to workspaces, instead of being created separately in each workspace.
concepts.example: The quality-analysts account group is assigned to cinderline-prod with USER permission rather than recreated there.

concepts.definition: OAuth sign-in in which a person consents in a browser and a tool receives access and refresh tokens that let it act as that person.
concepts.example: Maya runs databricks auth login once; later CLI calls reuse the cached token and see only what Maya may see.

concepts.definition: OAuth authentication in which a service principal exchanges its client ID and OAuth secret at the token endpoint for an access token with an expiry.
concepts.example: The ingest script sends sp-nightly-ingest's client ID and secret to /oidc/v1/token and receives a bearer token.

concepts.definition: Authentication in which a workload exchanges a token issued by its own platform for a Databricks OAuth token for one service principal, accepted only if a federation policy's issuer, subject and audience match.
concepts.example: Cinderline's CI job on the main branch exchanges its platform token for a token for sp-ci-deploy; no Databricks secret is stored.

concepts.definition: A long-lived bearer credential created for one user or service principal that authenticates API calls as that principal until it expires or is revoked.
concepts.example: Lena's PAT pasted into a committed notebook lets anyone with the repository act as Lena.

concepts.definition: A named container of secrets whose ACL grants READ, WRITE or MANAGE, read at run time with the permission of whoever runs the command.
concepts.example: Scope supplier-sftp holds the SFTP password; ingest-jobs has READ and quality-platform-owners has MANAGE.

concepts.definition: The principal whose privileges Unity Catalog checks for a request: the user for an interactive query, the run-as identity for a job.
concepts.example: Ravi triggers the nightly job, but the write is checked against sp-nightly-ingest.

concepts.definition: The point on a request path that refused or reshaped it: credential, workspace, catalog privilege, data policy, secret ACL or network.
concepts.example: A PERMISSION_DENIED naming USE SCHEMA is the catalog layer; an empty result with no error points at a row filter.

concepts.definition: A SQL function attached to a table that runs at query time and returns true only for the rows the calling principal may see.
concepts.example: plant_rows returns every row to quality-leads and only EU-1 and EU-2 rows to plant-eu-analysts.

concepts.definition: A SQL function attached to one column that runs at query time and returns either the stored value or a replacement of the same type.
concepts.example: inspector_email_mask shows addresses to quality-leads and [masked] to everyone else.

concepts.definition: Unity Catalog policies defined on a catalog, schema or table that match columns or tables by governance tags and apply a row filter or column mask to named principals.
concepts.example: One policy on quality.accepted masks every column tagged pii, including a table created next month.

concepts.definition: The system table that records account and workspace events with the time, service, action, acting identity, request parameters, source address and response.
concepts.example: A query on system.access.audit lists every getSecret call on scope supplier-sftp this week, grouped by identity.

concepts.definition: The interval during which a leaked credential was usable, from the moment it could be copied until it was revoked, used to bound the evidence search.
concepts.example: Lena's token was committed at 17:20 on 12 September and revoked at 08:05 on 15 September.

concepts.definition: Granting each principal only the privileges its task needs, on the lowest securable that works, and proving it with tests that must fail.
concepts.example: SELECT on one view for the supplier portal instead of SELECT on the whole quality catalog.

concepts.definition: Dividing a sensitive change so that requesting, approving, applying and auditing it are done by different people or principals.
concepts.example: An analyst requests access, the schema owner approves, a platform administrator applies, and security reviews the audit rows.

concepts.definition: A table of principal, securable, action and expected result, with as many must-fail rows as must-succeed rows, run against the real principals.
concepts.example: Six rows for the supplier portal: one allowed read, three denials, one row-count check and one masked-value check.

concepts.definition: Account access rules on a service principal: the User role lets a principal run work as it, the Manager role lets a principal manage it.
concepts.example: Only the release managers group holds User on sp-nightly-ingest, so only they can make a job run as it.

concepts.definition: The validity period of a service principal's OAuth secret, after which the token endpoint no longer accepts it.
concepts.example: A secret created without a lifetime expires 730 days later unless it is rotated first.

concepts.definition: The workspace permission that decides which principals may create and use personal access tokens, separate from any data privilege.
concepts.example: Only the automation group and admins hold CAN_USE on tokens in cinderline-prod.

concepts.definition: The account-admin action that makes a system schema such as access available in a metastore before any of its tables can be queried.
concepts.example: Until the access schema is enabled, system.access.audit cannot be queried in Cinderline's metastore.

visuals.alt: Where a bearer token leaks, and what revocation changes. Each path gives whoever finds the token Lena's grants, not a reduced set.
